title: Three Countries Team Up for a Giant Defense Pact — But They Say It's Just for Safety
summary: What if you and your friends promised to protect each other from bullies, but you weren't looking for a fight? That's kind of what three countries just did. Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey signed a big defense agreement on Friday in the holy city of Mecca. They call it the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement. The deal says that if any of the three countries is attacked, the other two will treat it like an attack on themselves and come to help. But Pakistan's foreign minister, Ishaq Dar, quickly explained on Sunday that the pact is "purely defensive in nature" — meaning it's only for protection, not for starting trouble. He said other countries can join too, as long as they agree to solve problems peacefully. The agreement comes at a time when tensions are high between the U.S. and Iran, but Turkey's foreign minister also said the deal is not aimed at Iran or any other country. So why team up? Each country brings something special: Pakistan has a strong army and is the only Muslim country with nuclear weapons; Saudi Arabia has lots of money and influence in the region; and Turkey, a NATO member, has a big military and makes its own advanced weapons. After the signing, people celebrated by lighting up landmarks in the colors of the three flags in Islamabad and Saudi cities. Defense experts say this isn't like NATO — it's a smaller club, but it shows these countries want to work together for stability. Pakistan already had separate defense deals with Saudi Arabia and Turkey, but this new pact ties all three together. It's a historic handshake in a tense neighborhood.
why_it_matters: When nations promise to protect each other peacefully, it is like a big friendship pact — it can help keep whole regions calm, which makes the world safer for kids everywhere.

questions.question: Which three countries signed the new defense agreement?
What happens if one of the three countries is attacked?
options: Only the attacked country fights back on its own.
The other two treat it like an attack on themselves and come to help.
The three countries ask the U.S. to help.
The United Nations solves the problem.
questions.correct_answer: The other two treat it like an attack on themselves and come to help.

questions.question: According to Pakistan's foreign minister, the agreement is...
options: Purely for defense, not for starting trouble
questions.correct_answer: Purely for defense, not for starting trouble

options: They lit up landmarks in the colors of the three flags.
They shot fireworks over the pyramids.
They held a parade in the capital of Iran.
They closed all schools for a week.

background_read: About 75 years ago, many countries created NATO, a defense alliance to protect each other after World War II.
When countries sign mutual defense pacts, they often do so because they share common worries or want to show other nations that they stand together.
Article_Structure: WHO: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey — their leaders and foreign ministers.
WHAT: The signing of the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement, a pact promising mutual protection if any one of them is attacked.
WHERE: The holy city of Mecca, Saudi Arabia.
WHY: To increase their safety and stability in a tense region, and because each country brings unique strengths (military power, money, advanced weapons).

perspectives.description: They see the pact as a smart way to be stronger together, protect their people, and send a message that they solve problems peacefully.
They note this is not a huge alliance like NATO, but a smaller club that signals these nations want to cooperate and bring stability to their part of the world.
They might feel nervous because a new powerful group is forming, even if the pact says it's not aimed at anyone specific.
